title: Sampling, Estimation & the Bootstrap
summary: Every metric is computed from a sample, so it comes with uncertainty. Learn the unbiased variance, the standard error and the normal-approximation interval, then Efron's bootstrap: resample your own data to get intervals for statistics that have no formula, and check any interval method with a coverage simulation.
takeaways: Use ddof=1 for the sample variance. NumPy's default divides by n and understates spread.
The standard error s/√n measures how much the estimate wobbles, and it shrinks with √n, not n.
The percentile bootstrap resamples the data with replacement and reads the interval off the replicates' quantiles, lower quantile first.
Seed and vectorize the resampling, and verify any interval method by simulating its coverage.

steps.label: Point estimate
steps.detail: Compute the statistic (mean, median, difference) on the observed sample.

steps.label: Resample
steps.detail: Draw a (B, n) matrix of indices with replacement from a seeded generator.

steps.label: Replicate
steps.detail: Apply the statistic along each row to get B bootstrap replicates.

steps.label: Percentiles
steps.detail: Take the alpha/2 and 1 − alpha/2 quantiles of the replicates as the interval.

steps.label: Check coverage
steps.detail: On simulated data with a known truth, confirm the interval covers it at the stated rate.

terms.definition: A rule that turns a sample into a guess for a population quantity, such as x̄ for the mean.
Dividing squared deviations by n − 1 instead of n, which makes the sample variance unbiased.
The standard deviation of an estimator across repeated samples. For the mean, s/√n.
An interval from a procedure that captures the true value in a stated fraction (e.g. 95%) of repeated samples.
Approximating an estimator's sampling distribution by recomputing it on resamples drawn with replacement from the data.
The fraction of intervals, over repeated samples, that contain the true value.
